idea-plugin.name: Astra
idea-plugin.description:
Astra: Local-first API client for JetBrains IDEs

Astra is a production-ready HTTP workspace that lives inside your IDE. Design, send, and debug requests without leaving the editor, and keep every collection, environment, and response on your own machine.

Key capabilities

  • Request workspace: method, URL, query parameters, headers, body, and authorization in one editor.
  • Collections and folders: organize requests in a shared tree with rename, duplicate, and delete.
  • Environments: named variable sets with {{variable}} substitution across URLs, headers, and bodies.
  • Response viewer: formatted body, headers, cookies, timing, and response size.
  • Tests and history: lightweight assertions on status, body, and time, plus post-response scripts that capture values into environments.
  • Collection runner: iterate a collection or folder with data files, delays, per-iteration results, and CSV/JSON/JUnit XML export for CI.
  • Import and export: Postman collections, environments and data dumps, Insomnia requests and full exports, OpenAPI 3.0 (JSON and YAML), cURL commands, and native Astra workspaces.
  • IDE integration: import .http / .rest files and OpenAPI documents, generate requests from Spring controllers, and load variables from application.yml.
  • Mock server: serve generated responses for a collection or an OpenAPI document on a local port.

Designed for privacy

Astra is local-first. Requests are executed directly from your IDE, and all workspace data is stored in a plain JSON file in your IDE configuration directory, shared by every IDE window. No account, no synchronization service, and no telemetry.

Getting started

  1. Open the Astra tool window on the right side of the IDE.
  2. Create a collection, add a request, and enter the target URL.
  3. Optionally define environment variables, then press Send.

Compatibility

Requires IntelliJ IDEA (Community or Ultimate) 2024.2 or later, or any JetBrains IDE based on the same platform version. Dark and light themes are fully supported.

Support

Source code, issue tracker, and release notes: github.com/baby-1223/astra-intellij
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.17

  • Spring controller generation now renders generic request bodies: Result<User>, List<User> and Map<String, User> produce real field samples instead of {}.
  • Kotlin data classes with primary-constructor properties and nullable types are supported.
  • Java parameter types containing generic commas no longer get truncated.

0.3.16

  • Fix SpillingKt compatibility error on IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+ — replaced Kotlin coroutine sequence with a plain list in SecretCodec.

0.3.15

  • Form Data rows support text and file types, so multipart upload endpoints can be tested. Files are sent with their original name and content type.
  • jsonpath assertions support bracket keys, negative indexes, wildcards and recursive descent.
  • Add extract token = $.data.token to the Tests tab to store response values in the active environment for later requests and the collection runner.

0.3.14

  • New Code tab after Post-response with cURL, Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, and IDEA HTTP Client snippets for the current request.
  • Snippets include resolved variables and can be copied with one click.

0.3.13

  • Collection and folder runner reports can be exported as JUnit XML for CI pipelines.
  • Import .http / .rest files and OpenAPI YAML documents.
  • Generate Astra requests from Spring controllers, including path variables, query parameters, headers, and DTO request bodies.
  • Load variables from application.yml / application.properties, deriving baseUrl from the server port and context path.
  • Copy requests as cURL, Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, or IDEA HTTP Client snippets.
  • Import variables by pasting .env / CSV text and copy any scope as .env.
  • Local mock server with generated sample payloads for documented and undocumented endpoints.
  • The collection star is now a drawn five-pointed star icon, replacing the text glyph.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: collections, folders, environments, HTTP requests, response viewer, tests, history.
  • Collection runner with data files, iterations, delays, and report export.
  • Postman, OpenAPI 3.0, cURL, and native workspace import/export.
